title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The sheet is the reverse of a typed announcement. It is a 30.10.80 notice for the Montpellier differential-geometry seminar: A. Medina, 'La courbure des métriques invariantes à gauche sur les groupes de Lie' d'après Milnor. Grothendieck reused it upside down as scratch paper. The typed text has nothing to do with the mathematics.

The handwritten part continues the previous page and is written up cleanly on the next page (175).

Setting.
- G = GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉ Ẑ, where u acts on λ by det(u)·λ. Write u_0 for the image of u in G and ζ(λ) for the image of λ.
- The central extension \widetilde{SL(2,Z)} (= B_3, the braid group on 3 strands, i.e. the universal central extension of SL(2,Z) by Z) maps to G.
- The map sends ρ̃ ↦ ρ_0 ζ(-2) and σ̃ ↦ σ_0 ζ(3). In effect this is the pair (projection to SL(2,Z), abelianization B_3 → Z). The central element ω̃_0² goes to ζ(12), reflecting Z/12 = abelianization of SL(2,Z).
- SG = SL(2,Ẑ)·Ẑ is the inverse image of SL(2,Ẑ). Inner action of G on SG factors through GL(2,Ẑ). So any α ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) acts on SG without choosing a lift.

What this page computes.
- An element β = u·b^{-1} (u upper triangular, cf. the previous page) acts on SG. The page computes its effect on the lifted generator σ̃ = σ_0 ζ(3); the symbol read as ξ̃_0 is most probably σ̃ / σ_0 ζ(3).
- The chain of equalities moves ζ-factors (twisted by det = μ) past σ_0 and g_σ. It arrives at the boxed formula ũ(σ̃) = ζ(ν' − ν'' − 2ν) σ̃.
- Hence u fixes σ̃ exactly when ν' − ν'' = 2ν.
- Next comes an attempted bookkeeping of integer parameters ν_2, ν_3, ν_6, apparently the central corrections for lifts of the elements of order 2, 3, 6. The page then gives a compatibility condition between two such lifts u, u'.

Purpose. Grothendieck is computing how the arithmetic/profinite symmetries (GL(2,Ẑ), and behind it Gal(Q̄/Q) via det = cyclotomic character) lift from \hat{SL(2,Z)} to the profinite completion of its central extension B_3. Here the centre is Ẑ(1)-twisted. This is the genus-1 / M_{1,1} level of the Teichmüller tower in the 'Teichmülleries' notes: one must track the central (Ẑ) correction terms when conjugating the standard torsion generators.
errors: The numerical relations '−ν_2ν_3+ν_6 = 2(2ν_3−3ν_2−6ν_2ν_3+6ν_6)' and '11ν_2 … ν_6 = 0' are only partly legible. They look like a trial computation, possibly abandoned. Their correctness cannot be verified from the image.

The intermediate lines contain struck-out terms and an index '2ν+1' that does not match the final boxed exponent ν'−ν''−2ν. The derivation is sketchy, and a sign or factor slip in the middle lines is plausible. The boxed result is consistent with the ζ(3)-twist of σ̃ and with the det-action, given the conventions of pp. 172 and 175.

ideas.what: Mapping B_3 = \widetilde{SL(2,Z)} into GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉_{det} Ẑ by (projection, abelianization). The generators are ρ̃ ↦ ρ_0ζ(-2) and σ̃ ↦ σ_0ζ(3); the centre goes to ζ(12).
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of B_3 as a central Ẑ(1)-extension of \hat{SL_2(Z)}; geometric fundamental group of M_{1,1} (or of the moduli of elliptic curves with a nonzero differential) and its Galois/GT action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (B_3/centre ≅ PSL_2(Z), abelianization Z/12). Galois/GT action in genus 1: Nakamura (1990s), Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the genus-1 Teichmüller groupoid and the SL(2,Z) layer, but not this explicit extension

ideas.what: The inner action of G on SG factors through GL(2,Ẑ). Computing the effect of an element u on the lifted generator σ̃ gives ũ(σ̃) = ζ(ν'−ν''−2ν)σ̃, which pins down the central correction terms.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting outer automorphisms to a central extension; central cocycle bookkeeping (cf. GT acting on \hat B_3 with the cyclotomic character on the centre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara (GT on \hat B_3); Nakamura (explicit genus-1 formulae)

missed.claim: Grothendieck works with an explicit model G = GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉_{det} Ẑ receiving B_3, so that the arithmetic action on the central extension is governed by det (i.e. the cyclotomic character). He then computes the exact central correction exponents for lifting automorphisms to the torsion generators. This is an explicit 1981–82 anticipation of the genus-1 GT/Galois computations later carried out by Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck explicitly handled the Ẑ(1)-twisted centre of \hat B_3 in the genus-1 layer of his Teichmüller tower. The content itself is close to known results.

deep.surprise_reason: These are scratch computations of central corrections for lifting automorphisms from \hat{SL_2(Z)} to \hat B_3 inside GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉ Ẑ. They are a fragment of a known Grothendieck programme (genus-1 Teichmüller tower) whose content later appeared in work of others. The page is rough and the ν_2, ν_3, ν_6 relations are inconclusive. The Milnor/Medina seminar notice is incidental.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'ξ(·)' should almost certainly be read 'ζ(·)', the same symbol as ζ(λ), the image of λ ∈ Ẑ, on pp. 172/175.
'ξ̃_0' / '\tilde{\xi}_0' is most likely σ̃ or σ_0 (with σ̃ = σ_0ζ(3)), continuing 'β(σ̃) = u(σ̃)' from the previous page.
The first line at the bottom ('ξ̃ = ξ, g̃ = g') likely reads 'ζ̃ = ζ, σ̃ = σ' or similar conventions for dropping tildes.
The marginal note 'σ_0 ξ(u) = ξ_0 ξ(u)' probably encodes σ̃ = σ_0ζ(3), i.e. the ζ(3)-twist of σ.
The last line read 'ξ(μ,(ν'−ν''−2ν))' is probably ζ(μ(ν'−ν''−2ν)): a det-twist by μ applied to the central exponent.
